title: Thumb and forefinger can lift a crumb by the first birthday
summary: CDC's one-year movement item is a pinch grip, and the example it gives is small bits of food.
body: On the CDC page for the first birthday, one movement item is picking things up between the thumb and the pointer finger. The example printed beside that grip is small bits of food. The thumb meets the index finger, which is a finer hold than a whole-hand scoop. CDC's standard for these pages is that the listed skills are ones about three in four children, or more, manage by the age shown. Those pages come from the National Center on Birth Defects and Developmental Disabilities, and the center says they do not replace a validated screening instrument used in a clinic.
